newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 24.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
BIHAR CHIEF MINISTER RECEIVES SETBACK AS MINISTER QUITS

Bihar chief minister Laloo Yadav received a setback when his minister for transport, land reforms and revenue, I.S. Namdhari, resigned. Namdhari said he would not quit the party and would instead serve the people as a legislator. Namdhari, in his resignation letter, said he was resigning from the council of ministers responding to his conscience. He said his resignation was not related to the animal husbandry case nor was it an attempt to put pressure on the chief minister to quit.
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS PARTY FEUD REACHES NEW HIGH

Infighting within the Congress owing to the organisational election reached a new high, with the Jagannath Mishra group in Bihar announcing a boycott of the polls. The group said the pro-Kesri group was indulging in massive rigging neglecting genuine party members. An upset Mishra indicated in Patna his supporters might go in for a parallel set-up in party chief Sitaram Kesri's home state because their complaints had been ignored. Meanwhile, CWC member Rajesh Pilot said he would not back out from contesting against Kesri.
The Pioneer
DRASTIC STEPS SUGGESTED TO CLEANSE BUREAUCRACY

Premature retirement and forfeiture of property were among the measures proposed by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances for tackling corruption and inefficiency in the bureaucracy. The department's recommendations were included in a document to be placed before the chief ministers' conference. The document proposed amendments in the existing service rules to achieve the objective of weeding out those who were either considered inefficient or of doubtful integrity.
The Economic Times
PLAN TO MAKE INSURANCE FOR FIXED DEPOSITS MANDATORY

The government is considering introduction of a clause in the companies act amendment bill to make it mandatory for corporates to insure fixed deposits invited from the public. It would aim at protecting the depositor against default by corporates. The department of company affairs had been receiving a large number of complaints regarding default in payment of interest and principal by companies. The working draft on the amended companies act had tightened the rules regarding acceptance of deposit by companies and also seeks to come down heavily on defaulting companies. The central bank had already proposed that public deposits with non-banking financial companies must be insured.
TISCO NET PLUNGES BY 965.8 MLN RUPEES

The Tata Iron & Steel Company (Tisco) reported a 17 percent fall in net profit to 4.69 billion rupees for 1996/97 (April-March). The 965.8 million rupee fall in net profit was on account of the provision of 730 million rupees for minimum alternate tax and higher provision for employee early separation scheme. The directors proposed to maintain the dividend at 45 percent for the year. The company's profit fell below market expectations despite the increase in production and rise in turnover.
VIDEOCON FLOATS $35-MLN RATE NOTES

Videocon International has floated a $35 million foreign borrowing programme in the form of a three-year floating rate note (FRN) issue in the international market. The funds are being raised for a 100 percent export oriented unit. The cap on costs was fixed at 200 basis points above the six-month London inter-bank offered rate (Libor). Sources in Videocon said the closing date for the issue had been fixed on May 30 while the signing of the deal had been scheduled for June 6. The deal, brokered by Peregrine Fixed Income of Hong Kong, comprises of a three-year issue of FRNs at par without any put or call option.
Financial Express
ON-LINE ALLOTMENT PLAN MOOTED

The Securities and Exchange Board of India has devised a plan to replace direct subscription to initial public offers with a system in which applications could be routed through on-line stock brokers. The terms of the public offer will be available on the terminals of brokers. Investors will only have to visit their broker and place the purchase order on-line. The offer will be relayed and the allotment made or rejected on-line. The subscription amount collected by the broker will be channelled to the exchange headquarters in the same manner as the member currently routes his securities and funds at the time of a pay in.
INDIAN FOOD SECTOR CAN BE WORLD'S LARGEST

India's food industry will double by 2005 and could be the world's largest if investments grew and the processing and production sectors were integrated, a study said. The study, jointly conducted by the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and management consultancy firm McKinsey and Co, said India's food consumption was expected to treble to 2,250 billion rupees by 2005, a figure larger than the entire manufacturing industry. The report titled "FADA: Modernising the Indian food chain" said the Indian food industry was now equal in size to that of the United States' and second to China's.
